static_traits.name: Zhang Yu
static_traits.educational_background: High school graduate; currently attending university on a soccer scholarship
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents and young siblings
static_traits.social_status: Have friends and teammates to talk daily matters with, but have not yet shared health and fitness anxieties with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before, and no psychotherapy received yet
static_traits.language_features: Frequently use catastrophizing expressions (like 'sooner or later will lack some nutrient and die'); tone negative, doubtful; can cooperate in conversation and willing to try new methods when encouraged

basic_info.main_problem: My obsession with exercise and being the best has led to health-related anxiety and fear.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because the fear and anxiety around health and fitness habits significantly affect my daily life and mental health.
growth_experiences: After receiving the soccer scholarship, felt the need to keep performing and looking the best; anxiety worsened significantly over the following months, becoming fixated on 'must be the best', and worrying that any slack would mean failure or losing the scholarship.

Pressure to maintain a 'perfect image' on social media compounded with competitive performance pressure, leading to daily repeated worry about whether the diet is healthy enough and whether there is nutritional deficiency, triggering irregular eating and overtraining.

core_beliefs: Only by staying perfect and the best am I valuable and safe
Once my health is not under complete control, disaster will strike

special_situations.event: When planning daily routines or actually eating, thinking about whether nutrition is complete and whether it is healthy enough
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the diet is not 'perfect' and 'fully controllable', severe nutritional deficiency will eventually occur with fatal consequences
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Make and strictly follow harsh diet plans, track intake meticulously, consider supplements to ensure 'nothing is left to chance'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Sooner or later I will lack some nutrient, then something will happen, and I may even die

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If training is even slightly imperfect, it means I am not doing enough, will get worse and lose everything
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Further increases practice, raising training intensity and frequency, to make up for any 'flaw'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am still not good enough, not doing enough; the problem will get worse and worse

special_situations.event: Posts content on social media or browses others' feedback and comments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my image is not the best, everyone will belittle me and not recognize me; I will lose opportunities and support
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly polishes and controls the online image, while proving themselves with stricter training and diet
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I have regressed / am not good enough

special_situations.event: Approaching a match/training assessment or thinking about scholarship retention
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Either the best or a failure; any slight imperfection means being eliminated and losing the scholarship
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids any possibility of 'failure' through extreme training and strict self-demands
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If this time is not the best, I am done for

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain steady recognition and a sense of safety through excellent performance and a perfect image
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failure, being denied and abandoned; worry that health going out of control will cause disaster (like losing the scholarship, even death)
defense_goal: Repress insecurity and anxiety through over-controlling diet and high-intensity training
Avoids exposing vulnerability to others to maintain the sense of safety brought by the 'perfect image'

object_relations.self_representation: A performer who must always be perfect, otherwise will be denied
object_relations.object_representation: Audiences/others who constantly judge and are disappointed, ready to withdraw approval at any time

object_relations.self_representation: An individual highly uneasy about body and health
object_relations.object_representation: An unpredictable body/environment that may bring disaster

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests recording fear, identifying thinking patterns, and exploring new methods
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worry these methods will be ineffective, thinking the problem is 'unsolvable'; subconsciously experiencing the counselor as an 'outsider who cannot really help me'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone hesitant, first deny then reluctantly agree; use wording like 'I do not think it is useful' 'maybe', reducing emotional investment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to consider sharing anxiety with friends/family and seeking support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If vulnerability is exposed it will be looked down upon or burden others, so rationalize non-disclosure as 'considering others'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasize in a steady rational tone 'do not want to trouble everyone, should not add burden to everyone', avoiding further emotional elaboration.

manifestations: Repeatedly worry that nutritional deficiency will cause severe consequences or even death
Treats health as something that must be fully controllable, otherwise disaster follows
outcomes: Daily life impaired (studies affected, eating disturbed)

manifestations: Bound by the inner rule of 'must be the best / must be perfect'
Difficulty allowing oneself flexibility and imperfection
Unwilling to reveal genuine anxiety to friends and teammates
Relationships revolve more around 'image and performance', making it hard to form genuine connections
outcomes: Reduced emotional support, subjective loneliness rising

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly states 'must be the best / must be perfect' to maintain the scholarship and image
Demands of oneself using others' expectations and online image as standards

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: After training repeatedly reproach myself 'still not good enough / not doing enough'
Intensely monitors diet and training; hard to relax

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Worry on social media that 'they will think I have regressed / am not good enough'
Attributes the experience of inner self-criticism to others' evaluations

positive_force: Has strong achievement motivation and self-discipline (can persist with training and diet management)
Has some social support resources (friends and teammates to chat about daily life with)
Has actively sought counseling to improve distress
negative_force: Perfectionism and high dependence on external evaluation form rigid conditions of self-worth
Cognitive biases like catastrophizing, mental filtering and predicting the future maintain anxiety
Overtraining and strict dieting as control strategies instead worsen anxiety and life imbalance
Avoids disclosing true feelings, reducing available support and channels for emotion regulation

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive exercise and strict dieting (control-type behaviors)
antecedent: When posting content on social media or browsing feedback
Near training / competitions or when self-evaluating performance
When eating or planning diet, worrying it is not healthy enough
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic cognition and perfectionistic drive regarding health and performance, and high dependence on external evaluation and approval
target_behavior.function: Temporarily relieve anxiety through reinforced control, gaining a sense of control and others' recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety is instead maintained or worsened; disordered eating and physical and mental exhaustion; academics affected, life unbalanced

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing worry about health and repeated rumination (health anxiety)
antecedent: When thinking about keeping the scholarship and future performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Predicting negative future outcomes and the rigid belief that 'health must be completely controllable'
target_behavior.function: Uses worry to drive self-vigilance and control, attempting to avoid losing control and failing
target_behavior.consequence: Sustained high-level anxiety and decreased concentration, affecting learning and relationships; difficulty relaxing and recovering

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding help-seeking and not revealing genuine anxiety to family and friends (avoidant social behavior)
antecedent: When asked whether they share their troubles with others
When thinking of seeking help or support from others
target_behavior.core_reason: Afraid of being misunderstood/looked down on or 'causing trouble for others', in order to maintain a perfect image and sense of control
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential negative evaluation and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced emotional support, subjective loneliness and accumulated stress; anxiety maintained
